//permission:
The workspace's rule, and the reason it lives here rather than in any package: `sed -i*` is denied and the same is true of a Python or heredoc rewrite, but the last of those cannot be expressed as a path pattern. The written rule is in agents/workspace.md and agents/principle.md; this is the part a machine can enforce.

V2 shape, and one thing to know before editing: this is ONE ORDERED ARRAY and the LAST matching rule wins. So `*` opens with `ask`, every exception follows it, and `sed -i*` closes with `deny` — that ordering IS the rule, and reversing the last two lines silently un-does the only hard permission in the workspace. V1 grouped these by tool and called the action `bash`; V2 calls it `shell`. A saved approval never overrides a configured `deny`, so no session can talk its way past refusing `sed -i`.
